body:
Part of #98.

## Why

`~/.config/hkb/boards.json` has exactly one reader (`serveContexts`, src/serve.js:128) and no writer
anywhere in `src/`. Every other piece of #98 needs a safe way to add a checkout to that list, so the
writer lands first, on its own, with its own tests.

## What

**Pure, in `src/model.js`** (next to `parseRepoSpecs`, which already parses this shape):

- `mergeBoardEntry(entries, entry)` → `{ entries, added }`. Appends `entry` unless an equivalent one is
  already there. Never reorders, rewrites or normalises entries it did not add — an entry a human typed
  as `~/code/web` stays spelled that way.

**I/O, in `src/board.js`** (next to `loadUserBoards`):

- `saveUserBoards(list, file = userBoardsFile())` — writes `{ "version": 1, "boards": [...] }`. Creates
  the directory when missing. Atomic: write a temp file in the same directory, then `rename` over the
  target, so a reader never sees a half-written list and a crash never truncates it.
- `registerUserBoard(root, board = null, file = userBoardsFile())` → `{ added, file, entries }`. Loads,
  merges, saves only when something changed.

Two things this must get right:

- **Equivalence is by resolved path**, `path.resolve(expandHome(p))`, plus the board slug. The real
  user list already contains `~/projects/pipao-v2`; registering `/home/…/projects/pipao-v2` must be a
  no-op, not a second entry.
- **A linked worktree is not a checkout to register.** `repoRoot()` (src/board.js:118) shells
  `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which inside a worker worktree returns the worktree. Resolve to the
  main worktree before registering, so `kb-96-1` can never end up on someone's board list.

An absent file is not an error — it is created. A malformed file keeps `loadUserBoards`' current
exitCode 2 behaviour and is never overwritten: refuse rather than clobber a file a human wrote.

## Done when

`npm run lint && npm test` is green and a new `test/boards.test.js` covers, under a temp
`KB_CONFIG_HOME`:

- registering into a missing file creates `{version:1,boards:[…]}` with one entry;
- registering the same root twice returns `added:false` the second time and leaves the file byte-identical;
- `~/x` and the absolute expansion of `~/x` are one entry, in both orders;
- an existing hand-written entry (including the object form `{path, board}`) survives a registration untouched;
- a malformed file throws exitCode 2 and is left on disk unchanged;
- two registrations of different roots both land (simulate by calling twice; the point is no lost update).

## Contract — siblings depend on these exact names

- `registerUserBoard(root, board = null, file = userBoardsFile())` exported from `src/board.js`,
  returning `{ added: boolean, file: string, entries: number }`. #98's init child calls exactly this.
- The on-disk shape is `{ "version": 1, "boards": [...] }`. A file that was a bare JSON array on input
  is written back in the object shape.
- `board` stays `null` when the checkout uses its own default — do not write `"default"` explicitly.
- Do not change `loadUserBoards`, `expandHome`, `userBoardsFile` or `parseRepoSpecs` signatures; the
  serve child is reading them concurrently.
goal: registerUserBoard() adds a checkout to ~/.config/hkb/boards.json idempotently and atomically
title: A user-level board registry that can be written, not just read
